issue.title: ESQL: Improve some validation/syntax error messages to be clearer

labels.name: Team:Analytics
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
### Description

Some error messages are really hard to decipher and it can make the edit query experience a bit frustrating.

Here some examples:

* [ ] incomplete command scenario error can be improved rather than report the raw syntax error: `from index | eval` => `missing {SRC_UNQUOTED_IDENTIFIER, SRC_QUOTED_IDENTIFIER} at '<EOF>'`.
  * Perhaps something like `Incomplete command sent: EVAL`  #100639
* [x] `stats` validation error can be improved when a token which may looks like an aggs function is sent without brackets: `from index | stats myVar = avg` => `Unknown column [avg]`.
  * Perhaps something like `Unknown column [avg], did you mean avg( ... )`?
  * The suggestion here is inspired to other `Unknown column [...]` errors where the field name is a misstype of an existing field/column name #100641
* [ ] In general the `mismatched input` initial part of syntax errors can be improved by something like `Syntax error`? #100639
* [x] `from index | sort <unsupported_field>` => `esql_illegal_argument-_exception - No TopN sorting encoder for type UNSUPPORTED`. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/100048
  * Ok, this is hard to grasp 😅 . What about `Unsupported column pass to sort command`?
* [x] `from index | where bytes` => `Unexpected error from Elasticsearch: class_cast_exception - class org.elasticsearch.compute.data.LongVectorBlock cannot be cast to class org.elasticsearch.compute.data.BooleanBlock (org.elasticsearch.compute.data.LongVectorBlock and org.elasticsearch.compute.data.BooleanBlock are in unnamed module of loader ...`. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/100049
  * I think this is unhandled. But something in the line of `Incomplete WHERE command` might be ok?
* [ ] `from index. | where now() + 1 year > 0` => `first argument of [now() + 1 year > 0] is [datetime] so second argument must also be [datetime] but was [integer]`
* [ ] `from index | limit 10 | eval now() - @timestamp > 1 year` => `[-] has arguments with incompatible types [DATETIME] and [DATETIME]`
  * On one hand the error message is not clear, on the other one I think that the query reads correct there. It can be rewritten in a "valid" way (`eval @timestamp + 1 year < now()`) but I think that it still makes sense as it is.
  * There are various combinations of this expression that makes it invalid as well, just try all permutations where one side of the comparison is not a datetime.
* Apparently using `*` (wildcards) in the query where they are not supported nests the error.
* [ ] `from index | eval abs(*)` => `error building [abs]: expects exactly one argument`
  * Same misleading error for any other function that is not `count()`.
* [ ] `from remote-*:indexes*` => `Unknown index [remote-*`
  * This is clearly broken somehow.
* [ ] Message copy inconsistency:
  * `row var = 1 in ("a", "b", "c")` => `1st argument of [1 in ("a", "b", "c")] must be [integer], found value ["a"] type [keyword]`
  * `row var = "a" > 0` => `first argument of ["a" > 0] is [keyword] so second argument must also be [keyword] but was [integer]`
  * Note `1st` and `first`
* [ ] `row 1 anno`, `row var = 1 anno` => `Unexpected time interval qualifier`
  * the wrong identifier should be reported together with the error message.
* [ ] `from logstash | where cidr_match(ip)` => `tql_illegal_argument_exception: expects at least two arguments`
  * This is broken.
* [ ] `[esql] > Unexpected error from Elasticsearch: illegal_argument_exception - sub-plan execution results too large [2.1mb] > 2mb` https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/138791

- [ ] INLINESTATS without aggregation

```
[esql] > Couldn't parse Elasticsearch ES|QL query. Check your query and try again. Error: line 1:47: extraneous input 'BY' expecting {QUOTED_STRING, INTEGER_LITERAL, DECIMAL_LITERAL, 'false', 'not', 'null', '?', 'true', '+', '-', '??', NAMED_OR_POSITIONAL_PARAM, NAMED_OR_POSITIONAL_DOUBLE_PARAMS, '[', '(', UNQUOTED_IDENTIFIER, QUOTED_IDENTIFIER}
```

  
These are some of the errors we manage to track so far, but will add more here if you prefer.

issue.title: ESQL: Graceful handling of non-bool condition in the filter

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

labels.name: auto-merge-without-approval
labels.description: Automatically merge pull request when CI checks pass (NB doesn't wait for reviews!)

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Improve the Verifier to handle queries with non-boolean expressions
 used in the WHERE clause (where 10)
In the process improve the readability of the Verifier class by
 extracting the checks into their own methods

Fix #100049
Fix #100409
